Machine Learning · Project 1

Spotify Songs’ Genre Segmentation

Grouping songs by how they sound, predicting their genre with a Random Forest, and using both to recommend similar music.

Dataset spotify dataset.csvTools Python · pandas · scikit-learn · Google ColabModels K-Means · Random Forest
32,833rows in the raw data
28,352unique songs after cleaning
6genres · 24 sub-genres · 449 playlists
60.6%Random Forest test accuracy
ObjectiveDataPre-processingAnalysis CorrelationClusteringRandom ForestRecommendationsConclusion

01Objective

Spotify recommends music by grouping songs with similar audio properties. The aim of this project is to build an automated system on the given dataset that does the same:

  • Pre-process the data and explore it with visualizations.
  • Show the correlation matrix of the features.
  • Find clusters of songs and compare them with playlist genres and playlist names.
  • Build a model and use its results for a recommendation system.

02The dataset

Each row is one song inside one playlist, with 23 columns in three groups:

  • Track information: track id, name, artist, popularity (0–100), album name and release date.
  • Playlist information: playlist name and id, genre (edm, latin, pop, r&b, rap, rock) and sub-genre.
  • Audio features: danceability, energy, key, loudness (dB), mode, speechiness, acousticness, instrumentalness, liveness, valence, tempo (BPM) and duration (ms).

03Data pre-processing

StepWhat was foundAction
Missing values5 rows without track name, artist and albumDropped
Duplicates0 identical rows; 4,477 songs repeated across playlistsKept one copy of each song
Release dateThree formats: 2019-06-14, 2019-06, 2019Took the first 4 characters as release_year
DurationGiven in millisecondsAdded duration_min
Scaleduration_ms ≈ 200,000 while energy is 0–1StandardScaler before clustering

Outliers in speechiness, instrumentalness and liveness were kept. They are real musical differences (rap is speechy, some EDM is fully instrumental), not data errors.

04Data analysis and visualizations

The six genres are balanced, with between 4,136 (latin) and 5,398 (rap) unique songs each, so no genre dominates the model.

What the genres sound like

  • Rap has the highest speechiness. Rap and latin are the most danceable.
  • EDM has the highest energy and tempo (median 127 BPM) but the lowest valence.
  • Rock has the lowest danceability but high energy.
  • R&B is the softest genre: lowest energy, highest acousticness.
  • Latin has the highest valence, making it the "happiest" genre.

05Correlation matrix

Values near +1 mean two features rise together; values near −1 mean one rises as the other falls.

Feature pairrMeaning
energy · loudness+0.68Louder songs are more energetic
energy · acousticness−0.55Acoustic songs are calmer
loudness · acousticness−0.37Acoustic songs are quieter
danceability · valence+0.33Happier songs are more danceable

Most other pairs are weakly related, so each feature adds new information. Popularity has no strong link to any single feature.

06Clustering with K-Means

K-Means is unsupervised: it groups songs that sound alike without being told the genre. The 12 audio features were scaled first so that each counts equally. The elbow curve has no sharp bend, so k = 6 was chosen to match the six genres and keep clusters easy to compare.

ClusterSongsSound
05,428High energy, fast, live-sounding; less danceable and less happy
17,322Happy, danceable, major key
23,347Very speechy and danceable (rap-like)
36,320Danceable and happy, mostly minor key
42,290Instrumental, energetic, long tracks (EDM-like)
53,645Acoustic, quiet, low energy

Clusters by playlist genre and playlist name

Each genre and playlist has one main cluster but spreads over a few. Rap concentrates in the speechy cluster and EDM in the energetic and instrumental clusters. Some playlists are much more consistent than others, with most of their songs in a single cluster. Genres overlap in sound, which is why a supervised model was also built.

07Final model: Random Forest Classifier

A Random Forest builds many decision trees on random parts of the data, and each tree votes for a genre. Combining 300 trees makes it more accurate and stable than a single tree.

Input: the 12 audio features, popularity and release year. Output: playlist genre. The data was split 80% for training and 20% (5,671 songs) for testing.

Choosing the model

All classifiers from the course were trained on the same split using the audio features and popularity:

Random Forest 57.0%
Logistic Regression 46.9%
KNN (k = 5) 44.9%
Naive Bayes (Gaussian) 44.8%
Decision Tree 42.2%
Random guessing among 6 genres (16.7%)

Random Forest was clearly the most accurate. Adding release year as an input then raised it from 57.0% to 60.6%, because genres belong to different eras.

Results on the test set

GenrePrecisionRecallF1Recall
rock0.700.790.74
edm0.700.740.72
rap0.620.690.65
r&b0.580.480.52
pop0.470.500.48
latin0.560.410.47
The model predicts the right genre for 60.6% of songs it has never seen, against 16.7% by chance. Rock and EDM are recognised best. Pop and latin are confused most often, because they borrow sounds from all the other genres.

08Recommendation system

For a song the listener likes, the system:

  • takes the Random Forest's genre probabilities for every song as a "genre fingerprint",
  • combines it with the scaled audio features,
  • keeps only songs in the same K-Means cluster,
  • and returns the 10 closest songs by Euclidean distance, the same idea as KNN.

09Conclusion

  1. Pre-processing: 5 incomplete rows and 4,477 repeated songs were removed, leaving 28,352 unique songs; release year and duration in minutes were added.
  2. Analysis: the genres are balanced and sound clearly different: rap is speechy, EDM energetic and fast, rock less danceable, r&b soft and latin the happiest.
  3. Correlation: energy–loudness (+0.68) and energy–acousticness (−0.55) are the strongest relationships.
  4. Clustering: K-Means with k = 6 groups songs by sound. Genres and playlists each have a main cluster but overlap.
  5. Model: Random Forest was the most accurate classifier from the course, reaching 60.6% test accuracy against 16.7% by chance.
  6. Recommendations: combining the clusters with the Random Forest's genre fingerprint gives song recommendations that match the seed song.

Possible improvements

  • Add lyrics or artist information to separate pop and latin better.
  • Use real listening history for collaborative filtering.
  • Try other clustering methods such as DBSCAN or Gaussian Mixture models.
